```{r setup}
library(mermaid2drawml)
```

## Introduction

`mermaid2drawml` converts [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) diagrams of any
type into natively editable Microsoft Word shapes (DrawingML `wps:wsp` format).
Unlike embedding a static image, the resulting shapes can be selected, moved,
resized, and reformatted directly inside Word, and each label sits inside its
shape.

Mermaid itself lays out and draws the diagram in a headless browser. The
browser reports every shape it drew, with its computed colours, line styles,
fonts and text layout, so Word output matches what you see in a browser,
including themes, `classDef`, `style` and `linkStyle`. The package integrates with
[officer](https://davidgohel.github.io/officer/), making it easy to insert
diagrams from R Markdown reports.

## Setup

Install Node.js (≥ 18) and npm, then run once after installing the R package:

```{r setup_node}
setup_mermaid2drawml()
```

You can verify the installation at any time:

```{r check_node}
check_mermaid2drawml()
```

## Basic Usage

### `mermaid_to_word()`

The primary function renders Mermaid syntax via the Node.js bridge and builds
DrawingML XML:

```{r basic}
diagram <- mermaid_to_word(
  "flowchart TB
    A[Collect Data] --> B{Quality Check}
    B -->|Pass| C[Analyse]
    B -->|Fail| D[Reject]
    C --> E[Report]"
)

print(diagram)
```

The returned `mermaid_word_diagram` object contains:

- `$xml` — the raw DrawingML XML string ready for `officer::body_add_xml()`
- `$scene` — what was drawn: `$scene$items` has one row per Word shape or group
- `$type` — the Mermaid diagram type
- `$next_id` — the next available shape ID (needed when adding multiple diagrams)

### `body_add_mermaid()`

For direct insertion into a Word document:

```{r body_add}
library(officer)

doc <- read_docx() |>
  body_add_par("Flowchart of the process", style = "heading 2") |>
  body_add_mermaid(
    "flowchart TB
      A[Start] --> B[Process] --> C[End]"
  )

print(doc, target = "output.docx")
```

## Using in R Markdown

In an R Markdown document, place the insertion code in an R chunk. The output
file must be a Word document (use `output: word_document`):

```
---
output: word_document
---

```{r diagram, echo=FALSE}
library(officer)
library(mermaid2drawml)

my_diagram <- "
flowchart LR
  A[Input] --> B[Transform] --> C[Output]
"

read_docx() |>
  body_add_mermaid(my_diagram) |>
  print(target = knitr::fig_path(".docx"))
```
```

> **Note**: `knitr::fig_path()` generates a unique path per chunk, avoiding
> collisions when multiple diagrams appear in the same document.

## Layout and Sizing Options

`build_diagram_xml()` (called internally) accepts parameters that control how
the diagram is fitted to the page. Pass these through `...` in
`mermaid_to_word()` or `body_add_mermaid()`:

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `page_width_in` | 6.27 | Usable diagram width (inches) |
| `page_height_in` | 9.69 | Maximum diagram height (inches) |
| `max_scale` | 1 | Largest size relative to Mermaid's own; `Inf` fills the page |
| `font_scale` | 1 | Multiplies every text size |
| `word_font_family` | `NULL` | Font for all text (default: the font Mermaid used) |
| `min_stroke_pt` | 0.75 | Thinnest line drawn, in points |
| `align` | `"center"` | Horizontal alignment of the drawing |
| `alt_text` | `NULL` | Alternative text (default: `accDescr` or `accTitle`) |

Mermaid's own configuration goes in `mermaid_config`:

```{r layout_opts}
diagram <- mermaid_to_word(
  "flowchart LR\n  A --> B --> C",
  page_width_in = 5.0,
  mermaid_config = list(theme = "forest")
)
```

## Multi-Diagram Documents

When adding multiple diagrams to a single document, chain `start_id` / `next_id`
to avoid shape ID collisions (Word requires unique IDs):

```{r multi_diagram}
library(officer)

d1 <- mermaid_to_word(
  "flowchart TB\n  A --> B",
  start_id = 1L
)

d2 <- mermaid_to_word(
  "flowchart LR\n  C --> D --> E",
  start_id = d1$next_id   # pick up where d1 left off
)

doc <- read_docx() |>
  officer::body_add_xml(d1$xml) |>
  body_add_par("") |>
  officer::body_add_xml(d2$xml)

print(doc, target = "multi.docx")
```

## Supported Mermaid Syntax

Every diagram type Mermaid draws is converted: flowcharts, sequence, class,
state, entity-relationship, requirement, Gantt, pie, mind map, timeline,
kanban, XY, quadrant, sankey, architecture, C4 and the others. Flowchart
node shapes that Word has a preset for (rectangles, rounded rectangles,
stadiums, diamonds, circles, hexagons, parallelograms, trapezoids,
cylinders, documents and more) become that preset; the others are drawn
from their exact outline. The README lists a verdict for each type.

## What comes out

Each thing Mermaid drew is one Word object you can select, move and edit.
The names show in Word's Selection Pane:

| Name | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `mermaid:node:<id>` | a node: one shape, or a group of its parts |
| `mermaid:subgraph:<id>` | a group holding the subgraph's background and members |
| `mermaid:edge:<a>-<b>` | the line of an edge from node `a` to node `b` |
| `mermaid:edge_label:<a>:<b>` | that edge's label |
| `mermaid:edge_group:<a>-<b>` | an edge grouped with its marker shapes |
| `mermaid:marker:<marker id>` | a line end Word has no end for |
| `mermaid:group:<id or class>` | parts Mermaid drew inside one element: a legend entry, an actor, an icon |

Line ends are Word's own arrow heads where Word has the figure, sized from
Mermaid's marker and reaching the node. Ends Word cannot draw (crow's
feet, hollow triangles and diamonds, crosses, sequence numbers, a circle
or diamond larger than Word's largest end) are small shapes grouped with
their line. Boxes crossed by dividers (class, requirement and ER boxes) are
stacks of rectangles, one per compartment.

Text sits inside its shape: click a box and type. Each label keeps
Mermaid's own line breaks and is never re-wrapped; the paragraph is
aligned as Mermaid drew it (a title stays centred, member lists stay left)
and moved with the text box's insets where it was off centre. Text that
belongs to no shape, such as an axis title, is a text box of its own.

To restyle the result, pass these to `mermaid_to_word()` or
`body_add_mermaid()`:

- `word_font_family` sets one font for all text, and `font_scale`
  multiplies every text size;
- `max_scale` lets a small diagram grow to fill the page (`Inf`);
- `min_stroke_pt` sets the thinnest line drawn;
- `mermaid_config` passes Mermaid's own configuration, such as
  `list(theme = "forest")`;
- `alt_text` sets the drawing's alternative text.

```{r restyle}
diagram <- mermaid_to_word(
  "classDiagram\n  class Animal {\n    +String name\n    +eat() void\n  }",
  word_font_family = "Calibri",
  font_scale = 0.9,
  min_stroke_pt = 1,
  alt_text = "The Animal class"
)
```

## Limits

- Embedded images and icon fonts are left out, with a warning.
- Hyperlinks (`click`) are not carried over.
- Text transparency is ignored, and gradients become flat colours.
- The hand-drawn look loses its hatching.
- Lines are not glued to shapes: moving a node does not drag its edges.
  Groups keep a node's parts together.
- Text is not re-wrapped: labels keep Mermaid's line breaks.
